sources.content: I think it's a coffee maker, but I'm not 100% sure. It starts brewing, then just stops mid-cycle sometimes, like it loses power. The weird thing is, it usually works fine the next time I try.

"It sounds like a common intermittent power interruption issue."

To help me narrow this down: is the power "loss" when you say "it stops," or does it just stop "mid-cycle" like it's pausing?

Also, if you know the general brand—even if you can't recall the exact model—knowing the general category (e.g., "a single-cup drip maker," "a single-serve capsule machine," etc.) would be very helpful, as that might tell us exactly what kind of component is failing."
Have you noticed if it stops during the heating phase or the brewing phase? I've had a similar issue with my coffee maker, and it turned out to be a faulty thermostat.

"A faulty thermostat would definitely fit the symptoms of a random stop mid-cycle! If we suspect the temperature sensor is failing, it could cause this intermittent 'loss of power.' Does it seem to happen more often when it's hot outside, or is it more common during cold mornings?"
It's pretty random, but it seems to happen more when the machine is already warm from previous use. It's a single-serve model, not the smart one.

"That's a very specific detail; if it happens more frequently when the machine is already warm, it strongly suggests a thermal expansion or sensor issue within the system that's only triggered when the internal components are already hot."
